source_findings: When theta_d equals theta_i, the ordinary front-advance denominator is undefined.
Dry-bin wetting-front advances are calculated at initialization by successive approximation for each bin.
An assumed Z_de is inserted into the Green-Ampt cumulative infiltration equation to obtain Z_d.
Z_de is iterated until |Z_de-Z_d| is less than 0.0005 cm.
The resulting dry-bin Z_d values are stored and reused whenever water is injected into an unsaturated bin.
The corresponding front storage volume is debited from water available for infiltration before advancing to the next bin.
Existing infiltration fronts use the improved Eq.18 before new dry bins are created.
If surface water remains and a new bin can take water, its initial delta-z is limited by the maximum advance during a time step described by Talbot and Ogden 2008.
The 2015 method therefore retains the dry-bin advance as an event/timestep numerical quantity rather than redefining it as an independent physical state variable.

architecture_binding.reason: A stored legacy Z_d table is a computational reuse device. Its derivation is tied to the dry-bin initialization algorithm and the infiltration time discretization, so a SWAP5 cache must not erase that provenance.

relation_to_qualified_gates.B2E_A: Qualified only the fully funded creation mass event with supplied initial advance.
relation_to_qualified_gates.B2E_C_R1: Qualified only atomic funded-prefix composition with supplied initial advances.
relation_to_qualified_gates.no_promotion: Neither gate qualifies the calculation of Z_d itself.

hard_guards: Do not persist Z_d as dynamic per-column physical state.
Do not treat one Z_d table as universally valid across changed timestep policy or changed hydraulic/bin parameters.
Do not claim code-equivalence to M2WC70 until the official C source has been inspected or an independently equivalent oracle has been frozen.
Do not infer partial dry-bin funding semantics from the source reconciliation.
